title: Proximity-fidelity request allocator: capacity-aware region affinity, latency thresholds, and staged circuit fencing
creator: Sasha Kim
description:
Goal: Implement a region allocation policy that (1) preserves low-latency regional affinity for active user sessions, (2) proactively avoids/evacuates overloaded regions before SLOs break, and (3) provides graceful load shedding via staged circuit fencing to protect global stability.

Background: Existing steering policies can route by simple latency or capacity hints but we still observe sharp SLO degradation during rapid capacity saturation (regional autoscale lag + KV cache warm-up). We need an allocator that blends proximity (latency fidelity), session fingerprinting, and saturation signals into an ordered failover/fallback plan while enabling safe rollouts and per-customer budgets.

Design overview: "Proximity-fidelity request allocator" is a lightweight, decentralized policy component that runs in the request fronting tier and emits a ranked list of candidate regions for each request. The ranking is computed from three orthogonal signals: (A) affinity score: weighted combination of client proximity and session fingerprint stickiness; (B) latency headroom: normalized distance to region 95th/99th percentile latency SLOs; (C) capacity pressure: region load ratio (active_tokens / soft_capacity) with hysteresis.

Key innovations/differences vs prior work: we intentionally avoid a global central decision plane to reduce decision latency; instead each fronting node maintains a small cache of region health vectors updated from control-plane heartbeats. The policy uses a "staged fencing" circuit model: when pressure crosses thresholds, we (i) softly de-prioritize region by multiplying affinity score by a degrade factor; (ii) if pressure persists, we fence the region for non-affine tokens (new sessions) while allowing a fraction of pinned sessions to continue for short duration; (iii) hard-fence triggers token shedding and fallback to next-ranked region. This staged approach reduces cache churn and KV-warming amplification.

Config knobs and parameters (initial defaults):
- affinity_weight = 0.5
- latency_weight = 0.3
- capacity_weight = 0.2
- soft_capacity_threshold = 0.75
- hard_capacity_threshold = 0.92
- soft_deprioritize_factor = 0.6
- pin_preserve_fraction = 0.15
- fence_cooldown = 90s
- circuit_transition_window = 30s moving average

SLOs & safety targets:
- Global p95 latency target for generation endpoints: 150ms.
- Regional error budget burn alert: >5% error budget consumed in a 1h window.
- Rolling region fence: limit to 1 region fenced per 5m per cluster to avoid mass-evacuation race.

Observability & metrics to add:
- allocator.region_rank[region] distribution for requests
- region_pressure_ratio (active_tokens / soft_capacity) time series
- fence_state transitions per region (soft->fence->hard)
- pinned_session_loss % during fence windows
- downstream token shed rate and fallback latency delta
- correlation dashboards: fence_state vs model 99th latency

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for ranking math and hysteresis transitions.
- Integration tests with local fronting + fake region backends to assert staged transitions.
- Chaos tests: simulate sudden 40% capacity drop in region A and assert single-region fence and no more than 10% global p99 increase.
- Load test with KV warm-up path to measure cache miss amplification and verify pin_preserve_fraction mitigates cold-cache meltdown.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged merge to fronting tier (start in canary cluster).
2) Monitor new dashboards for 48h; enable automated rollback if p95 increases by >10% or error budget alert fires.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% of traffic for 72h, then 50% for 72h, then global.
4) Post-rollback runbook prepared and tested.

Security & compliance notes: no user data changes; decision data is only region health vectors and session fingerprints (hashed). All metrics are aggregated; region health feeds go over existing control-plane channels (mTLS).

Alternatives considered: centralized coordinator (rejected due to added latency and single point of failure); pure latency-only hedging (caused capacity cascades in prior incidents); per-tenant global pin limits (deferred — track as follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Config knobs exposed in fronting tier and defaulted to conservative values
Automated unit + integration test coverage for ranking/hysteresis
New observability dashboards with guardrail alerts
Canary rollout plan executed with no more than 10% p95 degradation and no critical error budget burns
Runbook and rollback steps documented in Confluence

risks: Incorrect hysteresis tuning can cause oscillation and amplify autoscaler thrash
Pinned-session preservation may increase regional tail latency under extreme saturation
Feature-flag misconfiguration during rollout could cause partial deployment skew across clusters
Control-plane heartbeat loss could cause stale health vectors and suboptimal routing
rollout_plan: Gate behind feature-flag per-cluster; enable in canary cluster only
48h passive monitoring window, then 25% traffic ramp for 72h, then 50% ramp
If p95 > 10% baseline or error budget alert fires, immediate rollback to previous allocator
Coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams for enterprise tenant exemptions during ramp
